narrative:
The model has predicted a 31% chance that you will fail your final year, which is significant enough to require you to take remedial courses. This means that, based on your profile and the experiences of similar students, there are several factors that suggest you may struggle to meet the necessary academic standards.

The most influential factor in this prediction is your study habits. You currently study less than two hours a week, which is notably lower than many of your peers who typically study between two to five hours. This lack of study time can hinder your understanding of the material and your ability to perform well in exams. 

Additionally, while you have not failed any classes in the past, which is a positive indicator, the model suggests that your current study time is not sufficient to maintain that success. The desire for higher education is commendable, but without adequate preparation, achieving that goal may be challenging.

Lastly, your family support is a positive aspect, as many students in similar situations benefit from encouragement at home. However, the absence of extra educational support or paid classes may limit your resources for improvement.

Given these insights, it is crucial for you to engage in remedial courses. These courses will provide you with the additional support and study time needed to enhance your understanding and performance, ultimately helping you to succeed in your final year. Taking proactive steps now can make a significant difference in your academic journey.

Protected attributes sex, age and health were not used to make the machine prediction.
